name: LNK605DG-TL
title: LinkSwitch-II LNK603-606/613-616: primary-side regulated CV/CC off-line switcher with 700 V MOSFET
summary: A family of off-line flyback switchers that put a 700 V power MOSFET and a CV/CC controller on one die for chargers and adapters up to about 6 W. Output voltage and current are regulated from the primary side by reading the bias winding on FB, with no optocoupler, secondary control or loop compensation; it holds ±5 % on voltage and ±10 % on current. LNK61x parts add output cable drop compensation chosen by the BYPASS capacitor. The LNK605DG-TL is the 4.5 W (adapter) size without cable compensation, in SO-8C on tape and reel; protection covers auto-restart, open-loop detection, current limit and hysteretic thermal shutdown.

Tape and reel comes in 1 k pieces minimum for the G package and 2.5 k pieces for the D package; the P package is not offered on tape and reel.
The G package is offered for the LNK606 and LNK616 only.

notes: Adapter: least continuous power in a typical closed, unventilated adapter at +50 °C ambient, device TJ under 100 °C.
Open frame: highest usable continuous power from an open-frame supply with adequate heat sinking at 50 °C ambient.

The figures assume: DC input of at least 90 V at 85 VAC; a 5 V output with a Schottky rectifier; 70 % efficiency; discontinuous conduction (KP > 1.3); SOURCE pins soldered to enough copper to hold the SOURCE pin at 90 °C or less; 50 °C ambient for open frame and 60 °C inside the enclosure for an adapter.
More power is possible where a CC tolerance wider than ±10 % is acceptable, letting the SOURCE pin run hotter.

circuits.title: Energy-efficient USB charger, 5 V 555 mA
circuits.description: A primary-side regulated flyback from universal AC to 5 V at 555 mA with no optocoupler, built on the LNK613DG; 74 % average efficiency and under 30 mW input at no load. RF1 is a fusible input resistor; D1 to D4 rectify; C1, L1 and C2 make a pi filter for differential-mode conducted noise. D5, R2, R3 and C3 clamp the leakage spike on the DRAIN. The winding from pin 4 to pin 2 feeds FB through the R5/R6 divider, which sets both the CV voltage and the CC current. The winding stacked above it (pin 2 to pin 1), D6 and C5 make a bias rail that feeds BYPASS through R4, cutting no-load input from about 200 mW to under 30 mW. C4 on BYPASS powers the chip and, at 1 µF, picks the standard cable compensation. D7 rectifies the secondary into C7, with the C6/R7 snubber across D7; R8 in series with the 4.7 V zener VR1 takes the place of a plain preload resistor to meet a battery self-discharge requirement.

parts.note: transformer; primary pins 5-3, secondary 10-8, feedback winding 4-2, bias winding 2-1, NC pin unconnected

notes: With the E-shield transformer, meets EN55022 class B without a Y capacitor, even with the output tied to safety earth.
D7 may be a 1 A PN-junction diode at lower cost and lower efficiency.
Where battery self-discharge is not a concern, R8 and VR1 can give way to a standard 1 kΩ preload resistor.
R5 and R6 are standard 1 % values picked to centre both the output voltage and the CC threshold.

circuits.title: Flyback supply without bias winding
circuits.description: The same universal-input flyback on the LNK613DG with the bias supply left out: the chip runs from its DRAIN through the internal regulator, with only C4 on BYPASS. Bridge D1 to D4 behind fusible RF1, pi filter C1, L1, C2, and RCD-R clamp D5, R2, R3, C3 on the DRAIN. The feedback winding (pin 4 to pin 2) drives FB through R5 and R6. D7 rectifies the secondary into C7, and a 1 kΩ resistor preloads the output.

parts.note: transformer; primary pins 5-3, secondary 10-8, feedback winding 4-2, NC pin unconnected

circuits.title: Test set-up for leakage and breakdown
circuits.description: Measures BVDSS, IDSS1 and IDSS2. A 16 V source charges BYPASS through a diode and 4 kΩ, and feeds FB from the 10 kΩ / 50 kΩ junction through two diodes. S1 first ties DRAIN to the same supply while it powers up; then S1 opens, S2 closes, and a curve tracer between DRAIN and SOURCE sweeps the DRAIN I/V curve.
notes: Order: close S1 and open S2; turn on the 16 V source; open S1 and close S2; sweep DRAIN with the curve tracer.

circuits.title: Test set-up for output current
circuits.description: A flyback run from a 50 V supply to measure the CC output current. The transformer inductance is picked for tON × IFB = 2 mA × µs; RO is picked so the supply sits in its CC region; the output current is VO / RO. The bias winding feeds FB through 11.5 kΩ over 7.15 kΩ, BYPASS has 10 µF, and the DRAIN has a clamp of a diode, 200 Ω, a 200 V zener and 470 pF to the supply. A 3.3 V zener sits in series between the 680 µF output capacitor and RO.

operation.text: LinkSwitch-II joins a 700 V power MOSFET and a flyback controller on one die for low-power CV/CC chargers and adapters. It regulates the output from the primary side, reading the bias winding, so no optocoupler, secondary-side control or loop compensation network is needed. On the die: oscillator, feedback sense and logic, a 6 V regulator fed from DRAIN, over-temperature protection, frequency jitter, cycle-by-cycle current limit, leading-edge blanking, inductance correction, CC frequency control and an ON/OFF state machine for CV. There is no current-sense resistor. Overall tolerance is ±5 % on voltage in CV and ±10 % on current in CC.
The output follows a CV/CC envelope: constant voltage within ±5 % up to the peak power point, then constant current within ±10 % as the load pulls the voltage down.

As FB rises toward VFBth the supply leaves CC and enters CV, where the switching frequency is at its highest; this is the peak power point. In CV the state machine skips or enables cycles (ON/OFF control) to hold FB at VFBth. FB is sampled 2.5 µs after the switch turns off. At light load the current limit is lowered to cut transformer flux density. ON/OFF control keeps efficiency flat down to very light load.

In CC the output voltage, and with it the flyback voltage on the bias winding and FB, rises with load resistance; the controller changes the switching frequency with FB voltage so the output current stays constant. Inductance correction runs at the same time in the CC region.

The part runs in discontinuous conduction, so output power is proportional to primary inductance. The controller trims the oscillator frequency to cancel an inductance that is high or low. It learns the bulk capacitor voltage from the bias winding's on-time (forward) voltage, as the FB pin current during the on-time. The switching frequency can be set from 60 kHz to 85 kHz, which lets the transformer shrink.

LNK61x parts raise the FB reference as load climbs from zero to the peak power point, so the voltage at the far end of the output cable stays flat. The state machine's output tells the controller the load. The BYPASS capacitor sets the amount: 1 µF for the standard amount (a 24 AWG, 0.3 Ω cable), 10 µF for the enhanced amount (a 26 AWG, 0.49 Ω cable). LNK60x parts have no cable compensation. The output voltage entered in the PIXls design spreadsheet is the cable-end voltage at full power.

If FB stays under 0.7 V during the flyback interval, before the FB sampling delay (about 2.5 µs), for longer than about 450 ms (tAR-ON), as with a shorted output or an open loop, the MOSFET is switched off for 2 s (about 18 % duty). Switching alternates on and off this way until the fault clears, cutting delivered power by more than 95 %.

If the current drawn from FB during the switch on-time is below 120 µA, the part treats the loop as open (the upper divider resistor missing or open) and shortens the auto-restart on-time from 450 ms to about 6 clock cycles (90 µs), keeping the 2 s off period.
Die temperature is sensed; at 142 °C typical the MOSFET is turned off, and it switches again once the die has cooled by 60 °C (hysteretic, self-recovering).

The MOSFET current is sensed and the switch is turned off for the rest of the cycle once it passes ILIMIT. Leading-edge blanking (tLEB, 170 ns minimum) masks the comparator just after turn-on so capacitive and reverse-recovery spikes do not end the pulse early. A di/dt correction keeps CC from moving across input line.

During each MOSFET off interval the regulator tops up the BYPASS capacitor to 6 V with current taken from DRAIN; while the MOSFET is on, the chip runs from that capacitor. Consumption is low enough that the part can run indefinitely from DRAIN current. 1 µF or 10 µF covers both decoupling and energy storage.

LNK60x: 1 µF, rated above 7 V, any dielectric, tolerance ±50 % or better, placed close to the BYPASS pin. LNK61x: 1 µF (standard) or 10 µF (enhanced cable compensation), ceramic or electrolytic, with tolerance and temperature drift within ±50 %.

Including line, component spread and temperature, the output holds ±5 % in CV and ±10 % in CC over TJ from 0 °C to 100 °C for the P and G packages. The D package (SO-8) can see extra CC spread from stress in wave soldering or IR reflow; a sample build confirms production tolerance.

operation.topic: Bias winding for low no-load power
operation.text: A bias supply cuts no-load input power from about 200 mW to under 30 mW at 230 VAC and raises light-load efficiency, which may allow a PN output diode in place of a Schottky. Below 8 V output an extra winding is stacked AC-wise on the feedback winding so the bias voltage is high enough at the low switching frequency of no load. The bias capacitor is 10 µF of any type, rated above the highest VBIAS. Any cheap diode serves for the bias rectifier: FR102, 1N4148 or BAV19/20/21.

The feedback winding mirrors the secondary while the MOSFET is off, so leakage-inductance ringing on the DRAIN disturbs regulation. Overshoot on the drain waveform is acceptable; a large negative ring after it can raise ripple or degrade regulation. The resistor in series with the clamp diode is adjusted to damp the ringing.

Return the SOURCE pin and the bias winding to the negative terminal of the input filter capacitor by one Kelvin point, so bias winding surge current goes straight to the capacitor. Mount the BYPASS capacitor tight against its BYPASS and SOURCE pins and the feedback resistors right at FB. Keep the loop of secondary winding, output diode and output capacitor small, and give the diode copper for heat, more on the quiet cathode than on the anode, where a large area increases radiated EMI. A trace along the isolation barrier can form a spark gap with the output return to steer ESD back to the AC input; route the AC-side trace to that electrode well away from other traces.

The SOURCE pin copper is the heat sink. Hold the SOURCE pin below 90 °C for ±10 % CC tolerance; if a wider CC tolerance is acceptable, a SOURCE pin below 110 °C leaves margin for the RDS(ON) spread between parts.

Peak VDS no higher than 680 V at the highest input and full power. At the hottest ambient, highest input and full load, look at DRAIN current at start-up for transformer saturation and excess leading-edge spikes. At full power, lowest and highest input and the hottest ambient, keep the switcher, the transformer, the rectifiers and the output capacitors within their temperature ratings.

A 5.1 W board on the P package groups the input stage (RF1, bridge, C1, L2, C2), the primary clamp, the feedback resistors and bypass parts right at the FB and BP pins, the SOURCE pins on a wide copper area, the output diode with its snubber, the output filter capacitors and preload, and a spark gap at the isolation barrier.
